office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Three-term Republican incumbent Mark Klicker faces first-time Democratic candidate Kyle Palmer, a former Richland Planning Commission chair, after a 60% to 40% primary. Klicker voted against the 2026 income tax and says it will spread to everyone; Palmer says he is not troubled by the rate on top earners but wants a lean budget before new taxes.

candidates.summary: Three-term State Representative, farm-and-ranch realtor and timber producer who campaigns on tax relief, spending cuts and natural gas, hydro and nuclear power.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S3][S4][S5]
Says the state should cut wasteful spending and decrease the size of government [S11]
Pledges to rectify "harmful police reform bills" and back natural gas, hydro and nuclear energy [S1]
Voted against ESHB 1296 and the 2025 clean fuels bill [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (ESHB 2081) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; pledges tax relief and says the income tax will eventually reach everyone.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for cutting wasteful spending, decreasing the size of government and stopping budget growth.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 tenant housing-stability bill; sponsored a housing cost driver task force and small businesses in residential zones.

safety.basis: Pledges to work on rectifying harmful police reform bills.

climate.basis: Backs natural gas, hydro and nuclear as reliable energy and voted against the 2025 clean fuels program bill.

experience.basis: Three House terms since 2021 with a ranking committee post, facing a first-time candidate.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the parents' rights law, on House passage and final passage; no statement on notification or opt-outs.

tech.basis: Says the district's data center is already under strict state rules on power, water, noise and environmental review; proposes no new limits.

candidates.summary: Richland small business owner, real-estate professional and former Richland Planning Commission chair running for office for the first time, focused on housing, water, reliable energy and outcome-based budgeting.
highlights: Says the state should not make long-term spending commitments without a plan to pay for them and should judge programs by measurable outcomes [S2]
Says he is not concerned about the 9.9% rate on income over $1 million but wants a lean budget before new taxes [S3]
Would require data centers to disclose power and water use and pay for the infrastructure they need [S2]
Former chair of the Richland Planning Commission; no elected experience [S1]

taxes.basis: Not troubled by the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, but does not want to 'tax first' and wants a lean budget before new taxes.

spending.basis: Calls for outcome-based program review, cutting administrative costs and no long-term commitments without a funding plan, while protecting core services.

tech.basis: Would require data centers to disclose power and water use, pay for infrastructure and deliver local benefits.

experience.basis: First run for office with appointed planning-commission experience, against a three-term incumbent.
